findings.title: Task 2 breaks four existing tests it says pass "unchanged"
findings.description:
Task 2 (lines 43-45) adds four `SnapshotMetric` members, narrows `PythonAdapter.metrics` to the four 400 metrics, and claims the full `tests/metrology/` suite passes unchanged. It does not:

- **`test_snapshot_models.py:225-253`**: `test_json_round_trip_is_lossless` builds a `LanguageSnapshot` from four literal measurements. `LanguageSnapshot._one_measurement_per_metric` (`snapshot_models.py:190-193`) then raises "missing metrics".
- **`test_render.py:33-65`**: `python_snapshot()` builds a four-measurement `LanguageSnapshot` the same way, so both render tests fail at construction.
- **`test_python_length.py:60`**: `assert adapter.metrics == set(SnapshotMetric)` fails as soon as Task 2 narrows the set, and stays red until Task 25.

Every commit from Task 2 through Task 25 or 27 would carry red tests. Task 2 must name these three edits: absent-fill the new metrics in the two builders, and pin the explicit metric set in the adapter test. The success line should read "passes with only those edits".

findings.title: Task 4's Python fixture score (6) contradicts Task 3's counting rule (7)
findings.description:
Task 3 line 54 says a comprehension adds 1 per `for` plus 1 per `if`. Task 4 line 65 expects the fixture (`if`, `elif`, `and`, a comprehension `if`, an `except`) to score 6. A comprehension `if` cannot exist without its `for`, so under Task 3 the fixture scores 1 + if + elif + and + for + if + except = 7.

Line 63 has the same problem: "one test per decision point … each scoring 2" is impossible for the comprehension `if`, whose minimum is 3.

The conflict is inherited from the slice (D2 line 139 against Success Criterion 3 line 266). An implementer hits a red test and must change either the metric definition or the criterion. Decide which is right and fix both documents before Task 3 starts; the wrong resolution silently changes what gets recorded.

findings.title: Adding a required `complexity` field breaks positional constructions
findings.description:
Task 7 (lines 91, 96) adds `complexity: int` to the dataclass and says 400's tests are "edited only for the rename". `test_lengths.py:104-106` and `test_render.py:36` construct `FunctionLength("b.py", "g", 9, 70)` with four positional arguments, so each needs a fifth value.

The only way to honour "rename only" is a default on `complexity`, which would let an extractor omit the value and record a wrong score silently. Task 7 should state that `complexity` is required and list these call sites as needing a value.

findings.title: `Tokenizer` takes only file text, but the TypeScript tokenizer needs the path
findings.description:
Task 10 line 119 defines `Tokenizer` as "file text in, (token text, line) pairs out". The grammar is chosen from the path suffix (`_parser(Path(path).suffix.lower() == _TSX_SUFFIX)`), and the existing `FunctionExtractor` takes `(path, text)` for that reason.

With text only, Task 14 cannot pick between the `typescript` and `tsx` grammars. Task 15's `.tsx` JSX case then cannot pass, and line 160's rule that a file unparsed for length is unparsed for duplication no longer holds in reverse. Define `Tokenizer` as `(path, text)` in Task 10 and write Task 11's test tokenizer to match.

findings.title: `RecursionError` is not a TypeScript parse error; a recursive walk would crash the snapshot
findings.description:
Task 9 line 111 and the slice's failure-mode table say a `RecursionError` is "already one of the adapter's parse errors". That is true for Python (`python_adapter.py:81`). TypeScript passes `(TypeScriptParseError, MemoryError)`, and its existing walk is an explicit stack that never recurses.

Task 5 does not say the complexity walk must be iterative. A recursive walk over deeply nested TypeScript would raise `RecursionError` straight through `measure_parse_metrics` and abort the snapshot. Either require an iterative walk in Task 5 or add `RecursionError` to the TypeScript tuple in Task 7. Task 9 should also say which language its `RecursionError` test covers; today only Python has one (`test_python_length.py:178`).

findings.title: `MemoryError` is both a per-file token error and a whole-metric failure
findings.description:
Task 14 line 160 lists `MemoryError` among the TypeScript `token_errors`, which Task 10 line 121 turns into an `unparsed_files` entry. Task 10 line 123 and Task 11 line 139 say a `MemoryError` during the pass makes the whole metric `tool_failed`, "never a partial figure".

For TypeScript the same exception matches both rules, and the outcome depends on which `except` comes first. Remove `MemoryError` from the TypeScript token errors, or state the precedence and test it through the adapter.

findings.title: Task 9's function-set comparison is not observable from the measurements
findings.description:
Task 9 line 110 asks for the same "(path, qualified name, start line) set" on complexity and function length. Task 8 line 101 gives the complexity measurement only a `distribution`. Function length exposes rows only through `over_limit`.

The assertion cannot be written against the two `Measurement`s. Name the seam: compare `distribution.count` on the measurements, and assert the set on the extractor's `MeasuredFunction` list, where each row carries both values.

findings.title: "Marks every line under both windows" is undefined; D3's non-blank invariant is untested
findings.description:
Task 10 does not say whether a window marks the lines its tokens sit on or the whole range from first to last token. The range reading counts blank and comment-only lines inside a clone. That breaks D3's "duplicated lines are always non-blank lines" (slice line 169), which the file-length denominator relies on.

Task 13 line 153 ("different comments and blank lines report the function's lines in both") passes under either reading. State that only token lines are marked, with a multi-line token counting its start line. Add an assertion in Task 11 or 13 that an interleaved blank or comment line is not counted.

findings.title: A non-string `metrology.coverage_report`, and a bad value reaching `read_coverage`, are unhandled
findings.description:
`load_config` merges raw TOML values without coercion, so `"metrology.coverage_report" = 5` reaches the parser as an int. 400 guards for this (`preflight.py:111`, `_read_exclusions`). Task 16 line 175 rejects only empty, absolute and `..` values, and Task 17 has no non-string case, so the result is an uncaught `TypeError` instead of `SnapshotPreflightError`.

Separately, Task 21 re-resolves the key at measurement time and promises its only exception is `SnapshotIntegrityError` (line 219). The parser it reuses raises `SnapshotPreflightError`, and Task 22 calls `read_coverage` directly with no preflight. Say what `read_coverage` returns for a value the parser rejects.

findings.title: Task 29 can't be run as ordered, and leaves a store record nothing removes
findings.description:
- **Recording results dirties the tree.** Line 279 records each step's output in the slice design, which is tracked (`.gitignore` has no entry for `project-documents`). An edit between steps makes the next `sq metrology snapshot` fail preflight. A commit between steps 3 and 5 gives a tracked file a newer mtime than `coverage.xml`, so step 4 reads `report_stale`. Line 281's fix-and-rerun has the same effect. Tell the implementer to hold results outside the repo until step 10 and to re-run step 3 after any commit.
- **The scratch project's setup is unstated.** Step 9 needs it to be a git repo with a commit, ignored `node_modules/` and `coverage/`, and an identity (a remote or `metrology.project_id`). Without one, `derive_project_id` raises (`test_take.py:194-200`).
- **The scratch snapshot stays in the store.** `sq metrology snapshot --cwd <scratch>` writes a record to the real store. Line 282 removes the project but not the record, and `store.py` has no delete or prune. Point `metrology.store_dir` in the scratch `.squadron.toml` at a temporary directory.

findings.title: The 400-record compatibility behaviour has no automated test
findings.description:
The slice's Compatibility section (lines 246-248) and walkthrough step 10 rely on 400-written records failing validation, being skipped with a WARNING, and leaving other record types loadable. The code supports this, since `ValidationError` is a `ValueError` and `_iter_records` catches it.

No task tests it, and Task 29 line 280 lets step 10's check be skipped when no 400 record exists. Add one store test: a four-metric snapshot record on disk is skipped with a WARNING, a sibling record still loads, and `write_snapshot` for the same commit replaces it.

findings.title: Commit markers are written as checkboxes
findings.description:
All 18 commit markers are `- [ ] Commit: …` checklist items (lines 46, 68, 88, 97, 115, 142, 156, 171, 183, 191, 208, 229, 246, 262, 271, 276, 283, 290). They should be plain `**Commit**:` lines.

Placement is otherwise sound: each sits after its test task. The exception is Task 2's marker, which lands on a red suite (first finding).

findings.title: Task 28 leaves existing snapshot docs and help text contradicting the new behaviour
findings.description:
Task 28 adds the metrics and the config key but does not name these existing statements:

- `docs/COMMANDS.md:505` says each language "gets four metrics" and "Python measures all four".
- The absence-reason table at `docs/COMMANDS.md:520-526` lacks `coverage_not_configured`, `report_missing` and `report_stale`, which users will see in output.
- The CLI help at `src/squadron/cli/commands/metrology_snapshot.py:52` and the class docstrings at `python_adapter.py:102` and `typescript_adapter.py:19` list the old metric set.

Task 28 also has no Success line.

findings.title: `tool_support.tool_failed` needs a `command` argument the tasks never supply
findings.description:
Tasks 10 and 23 route failures through `tool_failed`, whose keyword-only `command: str` is required and is logged as "(command: …; stderr: …)". Neither task says what to pass for an in-process pass or a report read.

`tool_failed` also logs its own WARNING. A coverage failure therefore logs once in `read_coverage` (Task 21 line 218) and once per metric in Task 23, three times per language.

findings.title: Task 21 re-implements `files.resolve_files`
findings.description: `resolve_files(repo_root, [])` already runs `git ls-files -z`, logs ERROR and raises `SnapshotIntegrityError` on `None` or non-zero. Task 21 line 214 specifies the same logic again over `run_git`. Calling the existing function also settles where Task 22 patches `run_git`.

findings.title: Task 26 misdescribes `test_take.py` and needs a synthetic report
findings.description:
Line 254 says "real adapters, `FakeToolRunner` scripted as 400's tests do". `test_take.py` uses only `FakeAdapter`; no existing test runs `take_snapshot` with real adapters. Real adapters do work with an empty runner, because ruff and ESLint resolve to `tool_missing` when the repo has none (ruff is also looked up on `PATH`, so it may need a script).

The Task 18 fixtures list squadron and scratch paths, so Task 26 needs a small hand-written Cobertura file matching the test repo, plus a committed `.gitignore`. Say so, since CLAUDE.md line 53 applies to parser tests and this is not one.

findings.title: Task 11's repeated-token case only holds for runs of 101 to 199 tokens
findings.description: Under Task 10's rule, the window at index 100 of a run of 200 or more identical tokens does not overlap the first window and is a real clone. State the run length in the test bullet.

findings.title: Task 13's "function length is unaffected" is ambiguous
findings.description: An unterminated triple-quoted string and bad indentation are also `SyntaxError`s for `ast.parse`, so both files are in function length's `unparsed_files` too. Say what is asserted: file length still lists them, and the other files' functions are measured as before.

findings.title: Task 19 has no rule for a `filename` that resolves under more than one `<source>`
findings.description: "Joined with each `<source>`" gives two in-repo candidates when a report has several source roots, for example `__init__.py` under both `src/pkg` and `tests`. Both would receive the same lines. The slice's single `--cov=src/squadron` capture will not exercise this; record the rule (the candidate that is a tracked file) or the limit.

findings.title: Small test gaps against stated requirements
findings.description:
- Task 19 fails on a non-integer `number`; Task 20 tests only `hits="x"`. The failure-mode row names both.
- No test asserts that duplication's `counting` text carries the window size and ceiling, or that complexity's says module-level code is not counted (Success Criterion 1, D2 line 145).
- Task 21 treats a stat `OSError` on the report as a failure; Task 22 tests only a tracked file.

findings.title: Task 18's coverage.py capture will be large
findings.description:
`--cov=src/squadron` reports every file in the package whatever test subset runs, so the fixture is a full-package XML. `--cov=src/squadron/metrology/snapshot` still satisfies "captured from squadron" at a fraction of the size.

The README's opening lines say every capture is a `.stdout`/`.stderr` pair; update that when the XML files are added.

findings.title: Helpers the tasks reuse are private names
findings.description:
- Task 6 uses "`typescript_length`'s parser helper", which is `_parser`. No snapshot test imports a private name today.
- Task 7's read-and-decode helper is used from `duplication.py`, so it needs a public name under strict pyright on `src`.
- The existing read warnings say "for length" (`lengths.py:168,176`). Task 7 should say whether the helper or its callers log, or duplication will repeat a length-worded warning.

findings.title: Success criteria coverage, sequencing and stated facts
findings.description:
- **Coverage.** Functional criteria 1-12 each map to a task: 1 → Tasks 8-15; 2 → 9; 3 → 4, 6; 4 → 11, 15; 5 → 22, 26; 6 → 20, 24; 7 → 20, 24; 8 → 20, 24; 9 → 17; 10 → 11; 11 → 26; 12 → 7. Technical and Integration requirements map to Tasks 18, 28 and 30.
- **Scope.** No task falls outside the slice.
- **Sequencing.** Every test task directly follows its implementation task, and dependencies run forward (7 before 10, 16 before 21, 18 before 19). There are no cycles; `preflight` importing `coverage` creates no import loop.
- **Size.** Thirty tasks is proportionate for three metrics across two languages.
- **Facts checked.** `PythonAdapter.metrics` is `frozenset(SnapshotMetric)` (`python_adapter.py:105`) and `take.py:69` would raise. `_collect_functions`, `_extract_functions`, `_is_counted`, `_measure_source`, `measure_typescript_lengths`, `FIXTURE_ROOT_TOKEN`, `read_fixture`, `repo_relative`, `run_git` and `write_project_config` exist as described. `CHANGELOG.md` has an Unreleased section. `.gitignore` ignores `coverage.xml`, `.coverage` and `.squadron.toml`.
- **Load test.** The slice restates no NFR, so none is required.
